lessons: The premise finding holds. On Python 3.14, tempfile.TemporaryFile() calls io.open(dir, 'w+', opener=...), which emits open('/tmp','w+',O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC|O_CLOEXEC) before the opener's O_TMPFILE os.open. Carve-out (b) alone cannot make criterion 5 pass.

Revise the ticket Scope in, carve-out (b): also allow a write-mode `open` event whose path is an existing directory. Opening a directory for writing can create no file; the O_TMPFILE event that follows does the real work. Keep all other write-mode opens blocked.

On first use, tempfile._get_default_tempdir probes the temp directory by writing a random file there (the event open('/tmp/<random>', None, O_CREAT|O_EXCL...)). The ticket should have guard() call tempfile.gettempdir() before it sets the flag, so the guard never sees that probe.

Add a unit case to criterion 5 that asserts tempfile.TemporaryFile() succeeds inside guard() on the installed Python, which is 3.14.6 per the run log. Keep the blocked-case assertions in criterion 1 unchanged so the new carve-out cannot let real file writes through.
